title: Pullback of descent data along an fpqc refinement of a family is fully faithful
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: Let U and V be two families of morphisms with target S and let a morphism of families from U to V be given whose components over a fixed member V_j form an fpqc covering of V_j; the lemma asserts that the pullback functor from descent data relative to V to descent data relative to U is fully faithful (statement lines 8951-8972). The proof does not quote this from the refinement theory of the previous chapter but rebuilds it here: it first assembles the two families into single morphisms g from the coproduct of the U_i to the coproduct of the V_j, and then has to verify that this single morphism is again an fpqc covering, which is the only substantial step -- for each j the subfamily over V_j is an fpqc covering by the disjoint union criterion, so every affine open of Y admits a finite cover by affine opens of X, and the recognition criterion for fpqc coverings applies (proof lines 8975-8996). The rest is a comparison of four categories of descent data arranged in a commutative square, in which the two vertical arrows are equivalences because descent data for a family agree with descent data for the associated coproduct morphism, so full faithfulness transfers from the single-morphism case down to the family case (proof lines 8996-9011). The claim is H2: one genuine sub-claim is proved from a recognition criterion and the remainder is a commutative diagram whose commutativity is taken from the cited construction, so this is a complete but not multi-front argument.
